- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.6) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or near zero — model fails to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days — especially after sharp spikes or drops.
- After a price spike, model overcorrects and forecasts a sharp drop — then fails to recover, creating a “false bottom” bias.
- In high-sentiment periods, model overestimates 30-day mean — should adjust downward by 1–2% for sentiment >0.7.
- When sentiment is volatile or negative, model underestimates downside risk — should add a 0.5–1.5% buffer for negative sentiment.
- Model often ignores recent price momentum — should weight last 5–7 days more heavily in 30-day forecast.
- If sentiment drops sharply, model fails to adjust forecast downward — should trigger a downward correction rule.
- Forecast tends to be too smooth — should allow for 1–2% volatility in early days of forecast horizon.
